chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Jawhari, from his father, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

During the time of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, a newborn was born with two heads. Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was asked whether he should inherit the inheritance of two or of one. He said: 'He is left until he sleeps, then he is called out to. If both awaken together at the same time, then he has one inheritance; but if one awakens while the other remains asleep, he is given the inheritance of two.'

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Amir al-Mu'minin, Imam Ali عليه السلام, the authority giving the ruling
key_terms.مِيرَاثَ اثْنَيْنِ: the inheritance share of two persons
key_terms.نَائِمًا: remaining asleep, used here as part of the legal test

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali عليه السلام rule on the inheritance of a newborn born with two heads?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding a newborn with two heads and how inheritance is to be determined. The ruling uses observable signs of unified or separate responsiveness during sleep to determine whether the case is treated as one inheriting person or two.
